Bring your own bag boundaries

Source: vignettes/articles/bags-from-nso.Rmd
bags-from-nso.Rmd

Bags are the smallest rural administrative units. mongolmaps includes their names and codes, but does not include rural bag boundaries. Khoroos in Ulaanbaatar are available separately through mn_khoroos().

This guide explains how to use a boundary file you have obtained. It cannot display your bag map until you supply that file.

library(mongolmaps)

Check the available codes

Use the aimag and soum together when a place name is repeated.

bag_codes <- mn_codes("bag", within = "MN8401")
knitr::kable(head(bag_codes[c("name_en", "nso_code", "has_geometry")]))
name_en nso_code has_geometry
1-r bag, Alagtolgoi 1840151 FALSE
2-r bag, Baatarkhairkhan 1840153 FALSE
3-r bag, Bichigt 1840155 FALSE
4-r bag, Bugat 1840157 FALSE
5-r bag, Buyant 1840159 FALSE
6-r bag, Jargalan 1840161 FALSE

has_geometry = FALSE means the package has a code but no included shape. The parent code in this example identifies Jargalant soum in Khovd; use mn_codes("soum", within = "Khovd") to find other soums.

Obtain a boundary file

Ask NSO for a shapefile or GeoPackage containing:

  • A unique NSO bag code for each shape, preferably stored as text.
  • The date the boundaries apply to.
  • The file’s coordinate reference system.
  • Terms covering use of the data, published maps and redistribution.

You can contact NSO through its official website. Confirm availability and terms with the provider; the package cannot supply this file.

Read and check your file

The examples below are recipes. Replace the path with your actual file before running them. If you have a shapefile, keep its .shp, .shx, .dbf and projection files together.

bags <- mn_read_bags("bags_from_nso.gpkg", code_col = "nso_code")
khovd_bags <- mn_bags(aimag = "Khovd", path = "bags_from_nso.gpkg")
mn_map(khovd_bags, title = "Bag boundaries in Khovd")

Replace "nso_code" with the code column in your file, or omit code_col to let the reader detect it. The reader checks the codes, geometry and nesting inside each soum. If a check fails, inspect the file and its boundary date before disabling a check.

Use the file in later calls

Register the file for the current R session:

options(mongolmaps.bags_path = "C:/data/bags_from_nso.gpkg")
khovd_bags <- mn_bags(aimag = "Khovd")

To keep that setting across sessions, add the options() line to your .Rprofile. With the file registered, mn_admin("bag") can combine available bag and khoroo boundaries.

Join a statistics table

This recipe expects your own my_bag_table with a code column.

bag_map <- mn_join(my_bag_table, by = "code", level = "bag")
mn_join_audit(bag_map)

The joined data use the same columns as other package maps. Check for unmatched codes and missing shapes before drawing the map. See Putting your data on a map for the full workflow.
